topic_summary: The National Merit Excellence Scholarship provides ₹36,000 annually to eligible undergraduate students with at least 85% marks. Sources present conflicting criteria regarding family income limits, deadlines, and required documentation, while official renewal criteria remain undocumented.

facts.statement: Applicants must have secured a minimum of 85% aggregate marks in their qualifying examination.

supporting.quote: Applicants must have secured a minimum of 85% aggregate marks in their qualifying examination (Class 12 or equivalent).
applicants must have achieved a minimum aggregate of 85% in their Class 12 board examinations.

facts.statement: The official annual scholarship disbursement is ₹36,000 per annum paid in two equal instalments via Direct Benefit Transfer.

supporting.quote: Selected candidates will receive ₹36,000 per annum, disbursed in two equal instalments directly into the applicant’s bank account via Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

facts.statement: The official guidelines for the 2026-27 cycle specify an annual family income limit not exceeding ₹6,00,000.

supporting.quote: Family annual income must not exceed ₹6,00,000 (Rupees Six Lakh) as certified by a competent authority.

facts.statement: The official deadline for 2026-27 applications is 30 November 2026 on the National Scholarship Portal.

supporting.quote: Last date for submission of applications is 30 November 2026.

facts.statement: The official 2026-27 guidelines require an Income Certificate issued by the Tahsildar or equivalent revenue authority not older than six months.

supporting.quote: Income Certificate issued by the Tahsildar or equivalent revenue authority, not older than six months from the date of application.

facts.statement: Selection is merit-cum-means based with merit lists prepared at the district level by District Scholarship Committees.

supporting.quote: Selection is based on merit-cum-means. A merit list will be prepared at the district level by the District Scholarship Committee.

facts.statement: An unofficial guide claims the annual family income limit is ₹8,00,000.

supporting.quote: the annual family income must not exceed ₹8,00,000 (Rupees Eight Lakh).

facts.statement: An unofficial guide states an ITR copy of parent or guardian is the preferred document rather than an income certificate.

supporting.quote: ITR (Income Tax Return) copy of parent or guardian for the previous financial year, as it comprehensively demonstrates family income.

facts.statement: The applicant holds an income certificate issued by a village officer dated January 2026 and achieved 88% marks.

supporting.quote: Income certificate: I got mine from the village officer (Gram Panchayat level), dated January 2026.

claims.claim: Family annual income must not exceed ₹6,00,000.
claims.quote: Family annual income must not exceed ₹6,00,000 (Rupees Six Lakh) as certified by a competent authority.

claims.quote: the annual family income must not exceed ₹8,00,000 (Rupees Eight Lakh).

conflicts.note: S1 (official guidelines) mandates ₹6,00,000, whereas S2 (online guide) states ₹8,00,000.

missing_information.description: Renewal criteria, minimum performance requirements, and continuation rules for subsequent academic years.
missing_information.why_expected: Continuing scholarship disbursements across multi-year degrees require explicit renewal guidelines, but official sources publish no renewal policy.

missing_information.description: Appeal and grievance redressal mechanism for rejected or disputed applications.
missing_information.why_expected: Applicants facing document rejections or portal errors need documented escalation contacts and procedures.

coverage_notes: Official guidelines document explicitly omits renewal policy information.
